data.summary: Nevi & hamartomas · 7 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Halo nevus** (Nevi & hamartomas)_

**Q1. Discuss halo naevus — pathophysiology (PYQ).**
- Melanocytic naevus (usually compound or intradermal) surrounded by a symmetrical round/oval depigmented halo, due to immune-mediated (CD8+ T-cell) destruction of naevus cells and surrounding melanocytes — Sutton's naevus / leucoderma acquisitum centrifugum
- Children and adolescents, trunk (back) commonest; may be multiple

**Q2. Stages.**
- Stage I: pigmented naevus with halo; II: naevus becomes pink/lighter; III: naevus disappears leaving a depigmented macule; IV: repigmentation of the halo (may take years)

**Q3. Associations.**
- Vitiligo (in ~20–50% of patients with halo naevi; multiple halo naevi increase vitiligo risk), autoimmune thyroid disease, Turner syndrome, melanoma (halo around melanoma or distant halo naevi in metastatic melanoma — especially in adults; immunotherapy-associated leucoderma)

**Q4. Histopathology.**
- Dense lymphocytic infiltrate (CD8 T cells, macrophages) intermingled with naevus cells in the dermis ('naevus being destroyed'), loss of melanocytes in the halo epidermis

**Q5. When should a halo naevus be biopsied?**
- Atypical central naevus (asymmetry, irregular colour, ulceration), eccentric/irregular halo, onset in adulthood (>40 y), history of melanoma, change in the central lesion — to exclude melanoma

**Q6. Differential diagnosis.**
- Melanoma with regression/halo, vitiligo around naevus, halo around other lesions (blue naevus, Spitz, seborrhoeic keratosis, molluscum, neurofibroma, BCC), post-inflammatory hypopigmentation

**Q7. Management.**
- Reassurance — benign, spontaneous course; full skin and eye examination; photoprotection of halo
- No treatment needed; excision only if atypical; screen for vitiligo/thyroid

## Quick spotter facts
- Symmetric depigmented ring around a mole on a child's back — halo naevus
- Atypical halo in adult — biopsy (melanoma)

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Halo naevus). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
